text:
mike: Heads up — we have a growing island of stale metrics for user-facing agg_hours; looks like late-event ingest from EU region between 2026-03-12 and 2026-03-14. Need a catch-up plan. :thinking:

sara: how big is the window? can we just replay raw events or need recompute on materialized tables?

mike: raw events available at s3://ingest-raw/eu/2026-03-12..14. Estimated ~1.2TB compressed. Path of least blast: recompute pipeline to rebuild agg_hours + usage_counts. Avoid full parallelism — last run spiked redis and throttled model service.

alex: proposal: priority buckets + global rate cap. Enterprise customers (active last 30d) = high priority, others low. Run high first, then low. Start concurrency at 20 pods.

jin: +1. Also do a canary with a small time window first. Use windowed jobs (6h slices) so we can validate results and rollback easily. Example run:
```
./bin/recompute --source s3://ingest-raw/eu/2026-03-12 --window 6h --output-table agg_hours --concurrency 4
```

lee: infra notes: will bump ephemeral cluster autoscaler max by +10 nodes for the run, notify finance for spot spend. Set job TTL to 48h and enable pod disruption budget exemptions.

infra-bot: autoscaler request queued: +10 nodes for shard-eu-cluster, ETA ~4m. :robot_face:

sara: Console needs a backfill progress card showing windows done / ETA / error rate. Can we reuse the existing recompute trace events (job.started, job.window.completed, job.failed)? Need UX owner.

tara: I can own the Monitor card — will surface windows completed, tokens processed, failures and an ETA calc (processed_tokens / avg_tps). Will hook into job-state events.

alex: also we must gate this so it doesn't hit the hosted inference tier. Add a routing policy/tag `backfill` to prefer dedicated capacity and a per-customer throttle.

mike: agreed. routing policy example:
```
routing.policies.backfill = { "prefer": ["dedicated"], "fallback": "dedicated-throttle" }
```
And enforce per-customer throttles from recompute: 5 reqs/s to model service.

jin: ops checklist:
- create k8s Job template that accepts `--window` and `--priority-bucket`
- build priority mapping script (enterprise -> high)
- run canary on a single 6h slice
- monitor Console card + infra metrics (redis queue length, model qps)
- rollback if redis queue > 200k or model 95p latency > 500ms

lee: cost estimate rough: ~$1.8k per 6h slice at concurrency=20 on current spot rates. Flagging Finance for approval if we ramp beyond 24h windows.

sara: can we schedule the canary for tomorrow 09:00 UTC? Who owns verification and rollback?

mike: I'll own canary run and verification. Plan id=1901290000. Start with 6h slices; if 3 consecutive windows are green, ramp to 24h windows and concurrency 40. Will post results and a quick diff of aggregates vs baseline. :rocket:

tara: assigned tasks: tara -> console card, alex -> routing/policy config, lee -> autoscale + infra ops, jin -> recompute script and job template, sara -> monitoring QA, mike -> run & verify.

alex: envoy rate-limit snippet for per-customer throttle:
```
- name: backfill-rate-limit
  rate_limit: { unit: second, requests_per_unit: 5 }
  match: { header: 'x-backfill-customer' }
```

mike: noted. I'll also add a short smoke-check after each window that compares sample user counts to expected +/- 0.5%. If delta > 0.5% fail window and alert.
